question: Does clipping each task's gradient separately (X at 0.5, lambda*Y at 0.5) instead of one global clip at 1.0 keep Y72 held-out segment-exact at a mean of at least 80.0% over checkpoints 250/275/300 while X64 held-out acquisition continues?

design.only_variable: gradient combination: global clip 1.0 on (gx + 0.25*gy)  ->  per-task clip tau=0.5 on gx and on 0.25*gy, summed (combined norm <= 1.0 by the triangle inequality)
design.updates: 226..300 (75 updates), checkpoints/evals at 250, 275, 300, always stops at 300, one report, no retry
unchanged: SliceAdam, LR 3e-4, replay rows per update 2, expert union
restored v2 state incl. RNG and router
design.paired_controls: observed lambda 0.25 global-clip trajectory (control) and observed lambda 0.5 global-clip trajectory: non-gating comparisons only
design.single_seed_caveat: one run, one seed. Single-checkpoint Y72 SD ~5.3 segments; mean-of-3 SD ~3-4 segments; MDE of the mean-of-3 vs 160 is 7.6-9.8 segments (3.8-4.9 pp) at one-sided alpha 0.05 and power 0.8

arithmetic.rule: integer cross-multiplication only; no float, no rounding
arithmetic.operators: >= for every floor and for the gain threshold

R_retention.text: SUM over checkpoints 250, 275, 300 of Y72 held-out segment-exact >= 480 (mean >= 160/200 = 80.0%) AND every checkpoint >= 72.0% (>= 144/200)
R_retention.justification: noise floor: one checkpoint has SD ~5.3 segments (binomial 5.66, churn model 5.2, within-item 5.3), so the old 'every checkpoint >= 160' rule fails a model whose true level is 168 about 7-19% of the time (fully correlated .. independent checkpoints, SD 5.66) and passes one at 156 about 2-27%; the three-checkpoint mean has SD ~3.1-3.9 (cluster bootstrap 3.7-3.95), which makes 'sum >= 480' fail a true-168 model 0.4-6% and pass a true-152 model 0.5-7%. The 144 guard only catches collapse.

A_acquisition.text: X64 held-out segment-exact >= 11 at EVERY checkpoint AND X64 held-out token gain 225->300 >= 7.0 pp (tokens_correct(300) >= 1553 of 1920, from 1418)
A_acquisition.justification: control gained 14.0 pp (1687), lambda 0.5 gained 10.4 pp (1618); the real one-step probe shows the per-task clip makes about 0.60x (mean ratio of actual X-loss decrease, 12 steps) the X progress of the global clip, so 7.0 pp = 50% of the control gain keeps the gate non-trivial without demanding the control's pace

N_nonregression.text: X32 held-out segment-exact >= 40.0% (>= 128/320) and X109 >= 75.0% (>= 90/120) at EVERY checkpoint
